cases.description: Verify that getId() returns the exact id string that was supplied to the JsonSchema constructor (normal non‑empty value).
Verify that getId() correctly returns an empty string when the JsonSchema was constructed with an empty id.
Verify that getId() returns null when the JsonSchema was constructed with a null id (allowed because the field is final but may be null).
Verify that getId() returns a complex URI‑like id containing special characters and a fragment identifier.
Verify that getId() correctly returns a long id string (100+ characters) without truncation or alteration.
Call getId() twice on the same JsonSchema instance and ensure both calls return the identical string, confirming the id field is immutable after construction.
Verify that getId() returns an id containing a full range of punctuation and special symbols without alteration.
Verify that getId() correctly returns an id that includes percent‑encoded characters (e.g., space encoded as %20).
Confirm that leading whitespace characters are preserved in the returned id.
Confirm that trailing whitespace characters are preserved in the returned id.
Confirm that both leading and trailing whitespace are preserved.
Validate that getId() returns an id containing Japanese characters without corruption.
Validate that getId() returns an id containing emoji characters correctly.
Validate that getId() returns an id with accented Latin characters and diacritics.
Call toString() on the JsonSchema instance first, then call getId(); ensure the id remains unchanged.
Invoke walk(JsonNode) on the schema (or any other non‑mutating method) before getId(); verify the id is still the original value.
Spawn multiple threads that simultaneously invoke getId() on the same JsonSchema instance; all should receive the identical id value, demonstrating thread‑safety of the getter.
Calling getId() on a null JsonSchema reference should throw a NullPointerException, as the instance method cannot be invoked without an object.
